@NaveenGRao sold Nervana to Intel and MosaicML to Databricks. His third company, @unconvai, is building something that looks nothing like a GPU. His argument: AI is now limited by energy, so the number that matters is joules per token. Getting there means dropping the von Neumann split between memory and compute and building a machine that is "programmed by weights." To learn fast, they tape out a new chip roughly every three months. Their first test chip, a system of coupled oscillators, generated small images at about 900 nanojoules each, against about 50 millijoules on a GPU. @dylan522p asks why so many analog chips blew their lead once you count the conversion costs, whether programmability still matters when NVIDIA is king, and whether we will stop buying computers and start buying intelligence tokens. SpaceX has agreed to forgo $738 million in U.S. federal broadband subsidies and instead provide free @Starlink hardware to eligible American households. NTIA: "To ensure that no consumer at a Covered BSL is left behind, the provider (SpaceX) will serve the covered BSLs as this agreement provides. This includes providing customer premises equipment at no cost to new subscribers, so that households at covered BSL do not face the upfront equipment costs. Additionally, the provider’s broadband service will be subject to the same delivery timelines and performance testing requirements applicable to all recipients of BEAD funds." Under the new agreement, SpaceX would: • Provide free Starlink hardware to eligible households. • Guarantee minimum download speeds of 100 Mbps and upload speeds of 20 Mbps. • Offer a low-cost monthly internet plan. • Commit to providing service for 10 years. • Continue to comply with federal performance testing requirements. The agreement will save American taxpayers hundreds of millions of dollars while accelerating high-speed internet access in underserved rural communities. In exchange, SpaceX would be exempt from most BEAD-related financial audits, procurement requirements and administrative reporting, while remaining subject to network performance testing.

Analysis of Jensen Huang's return as Nvidia CEO: 1. Uncertainty removed: Mainly company strategy, product roadmap, tech development, and supply chain management. This overhang weighed on tech stocks over the past 1–2 weeks, so shares surged as soon as it was removed. But whether they return to prior highs depends not only on each company's position in the AI supply chain and Nvidia's ecosystem, but also on the two points below. 2. Uncertainties that remain: (1) Sales: The impact on Nvidia's shipments and revenue after tighter US controls on AI GPU exports and overseas compute leasing. (2) Circular financing: The impact of higher compliance costs and stricter reviews on ongoing and future deals. (3) Investigations, lawsuits, and stricter oversight: Jensen and Nvidia are still under investigation. Future public comments, internal decisions, and external interactions will all become part of the investigation and new evidence for questioning. This also adds to the sales and circular financing uncertainty above. 3. Real-world bottlenecks that can't be changed: (1) Data center buildout challenges (power, labor, etc.) and stricter related regulations ahead. (2) CSP capex peaking one by one in 2027–2028. (3) Manufacturing tech limits (e.g., next-gen advanced packaging yields).

黃仁勳恢復 Nvidia CEO 職位的分析： 1. 被移除的不確定性： 主要是公司策略、產品規劃、技術發展與供應鏈管理等。上述不確定性曾在過去 1-2 週對科技股造成壓力，因此不確定性被移除後股價立刻大漲。但能否回到過去股價高點，除了取決於個別公司在 AI 供應鏈與 Nvidia 生態體系的定位外，還要看以下兩點。 2. 仍存在的不確定性： (1) 銷售面：在美國更嚴格管制 AI GPU 出口與海外算力租賃後，對 Nvidia 出貨與營收造成的影響。 (2) 循環融資：更高合規成本與更嚴格審核機制下，對進行中的循環融資與未來新案的影響。 (3) 調查訴訟與更嚴格的監管：黃仁勳與 Nvidia 仍在接受調查中，未來的公開發言、內部決策與對外互動，都會被納入後續調查並成為質詢的新證據，而這也會強化上述銷售面與循環融資的不確定性。 3. 無法被改變的現實瓶頸： (1) 資料中心建置的挑戰 (包括供電、人力等)，與未來相關法規更趨於嚴格。 (2) CSP 資本支出陸續在 2027‒2028 見頂。 (3) 製造技術限制 (如次世代先進封裝良率等)。
